Note::deduplicate¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::deduplicate() const
Note Note::deduplicate(std::int64_t dim) const

Keep The First Occurrence Of Each Value Or Slice¶

deduplicate() removes repeated cells from the flattened row-major sequence while preserving the first-seen order of the survivors. deduplicate(dim) instead compares complete slices along one axis, keeps the first occurrence of each slice, and preserves rank plus all unaffected extents.

This is not an alias for unique(). Both use exact byte equality, but unique sorts its survivors whereas deduplicate preserves encounter order. Choose deduplicate when order itself carries meaning, such as a first-observed vocabulary or an ordered sequence of records.

On a matrix, axis zero means whole rows and axis one means whole columns. Negative axes normalize normally; deduplicate(-1) is axis-aware, while the no-argument overload flattens. Equality is collision-safe and compares every cell in a candidate slice. The result shares cell storage, supports text and bytes mode, and allocates only result metadata and distinctness bookkeeping.

Undefined input remains undefined. Invalid axes reject. Empty-slice behavior matches set identity: several structurally empty slices are equal and reduce to their first representative.

Example 1: Flatten And Preserve First-Seen Order¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "2", "a", "1", "b", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{3, 2});
std::cout << "flattened\n"
          << pluss::note::print(rows.deduplicate()) << '\n';

Output¶

flattened
Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["b", "2", "a", "1"]

The second "b" and "2" disappear without reordering the first four cells.

Example 2: Keep First-Seen Whole Rows¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "2", "a", "1", "b", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{3, 2});
std::cout << "whole rows\n"
          << pluss::note::print(rows.deduplicate(0)) << '\n';

Output¶

whole rows
Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["b", "2"], 
  ["a", "1"]
]

Example 3: Keep First-Seen Whole Columns¶

const auto columns = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "a", "b", "2", "1", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3});
std::cout << "whole columns\n"
          << pluss::note::print(columns.deduplicate(-1)) << '\n';

Output¶

whole columns
Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["b", "a"], 
  ["2", "1"]
]

The first and third columns match, so the first is retained before the middle column.

Example 4: Structurally Empty Slices Are Equal¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 3, 0});
std::cout << "three equal empty slices\n"
          << pluss::note::print(empty.deduplicate(1)) << '\n';

Output¶

three equal empty slices
Note(shape=[2, 1, 0], dim=3, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 5: Bytes Mode Retains Encounter Order¶

const auto raw = pluss::note::bytes(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "a", "b"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{3});
std::cout << "raw bytes\n"
          << pluss::note::print(raw.deduplicate()) << '\n';

Output¶

raw bytes
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=bytes)
[b"b", b"a"]

Example 6: Undefined Propagates¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined deduplicate defined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().deduplicate().defined() << '\n';

Output¶

undefined deduplicate defined=false

Example 7: Invalid Axes Reject¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "2", "a", "1", "b", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{3, 2});
try { (void)rows.deduplicate(2); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "deduplicate axis 2: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

deduplicate axis 2: rejected

See Also¶

  • unique: sort distinct values or slices.

  • sort: order lanes without removing repetitions.

  • vector: flatten to borrowed views without removing repetitions.
